: JUDGMENT :

The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the common arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No.
LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/33/2012-13 dated 22.01.2021 pertaining to Sy. No.25/4A measuring 606.80 Square feet of Venkatala village, Yelahanka Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluka.
.2.

The definite case of the petitioner is that the property measuring 606.80 Sq. feet in Sy. No. 25/4A of Venkatala village has been acquired under Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 02.07.2010.
The respondent No.3 has passed the award on 24.05.2011 and awarded a total compensation amount of Rs.7,97,335/- which has been received by the respondent No.1 under protest.
Subsequently, on 17.05.2012 the respondent No. 1 has filed the application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.8,000/- per Sq. feet from the date of notification.

Accordingly, the application is taken by the respondent No.2 for consideration.
A.P. No.129/2022 .3.

Thereafter, the Arbitrator hold an inquiry and passed order in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/43,106,44,33,72,107/2012-13 dated 22.01.2021.
.4.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting aside the following:

sentences.text: The petitioner claims that the impugned award passed by the respondent No. 2 is perverse, patently illegal, capricious and goes against the fundamentals of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

The respondent No.2 has grossly erred in not following the provisions of NH Act i.e., Section 3G(7)(a), the substantive law while passing the impugned award which is contrary to the provisions of Section 28 of A and C Act.

The respondent No.2 has not made any attempt to investigate the market value of the subject lands as on the date of Preliminary Notification and for the purpose of enhancement of compensation, the respondent No.2 has relied upon the notification bearing No. CVC/19/2010-11 dated 21.09.2011 and the said notification has come into effect from 26.09.2011, while the date of Preliminary A.P. No.129/2021 Notification in case of subject acquisition in Venkatala village was 09.12.2009 and hence, the respondent No. 2 could not have relied upon a notification which came into effect after a lapse of 1  years from the date of publication of Preliminary Notification.

Further the impugned Arbitral Award has added 50% on the guidance value of Rs. 1,500/- per Square feet on the ground that the special instruction to the aforesaid notification provides for addition of 50% for such lands abutting National Highway and thereafter the respondent No. 2 has once again added 25% on the guidance value without assigning any reasons and arrived at Rs. 2,626/- per Sq. feet.
There are manifest errors in the impugned Arbitral Award and consequently the same is liable to be set aside under Section 34(2A) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

The respondent No.2 has not assigned any reasons for redetermining the compensation amount at Rs. 5,25,00,000/- per acre especially when the parties had neither agreed that no reasons were to be given nor the impugned Arbitral Award is an award on agreed terms under Section 30 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act and among grounds, prayed for relief claimed in the petition.

The respondent No. 1 to 3 though served with the notice, not chosen to appear before this Court to resist the petition and hence, the respondents 2 and 3 were placed exparte and LRs of respondent No. 1 were absent.
The entire records in LAQ/ARB/NH- 7/CR/33/2012-13 dated 22.01.2021 secured from the Arbitrator.

.6. On the basis of above, the points for consideration are as under:
1) Whether the impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?
2) What order or award?

Perused the materials on record, on that basis my findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 : In the affirmative Point No.2 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS .8. POINT No.1:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note admitted and undisputed facts in this case.
The LRs of respondent No.1 are the owners of the land in Survey.

No.25/4A measuring to an extent of 606.80 Square feet of Venkatala village and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-7 under Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 02.07.2010 is an admitted fact.

It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the respondent No.3/Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India being a SLAO determined the compensation at Rs.1,314/- per Square feet for the acquired land.

sentences.text:
It is also admitted and undisputed fact that the A.P. No.129/2022 awarded compensation of Rs. 7,97,335/- has been disbursed to the LRs of respondent No. 1.
.9.

Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the respondent No. 1 filed an application on 17.05.2012 before the respondent No. 2 claiming that he is entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs. 8,000/-per Square feet.

On basis of the said application, the respondent No. 2 hold an enquiry and passed order in LAQ /
ARB / NH-7 / CR / 43, 106, 44, 33, 72, 107/2012-13 dated 22.01.2021.The respondent No. 2 has held that the guidance value of NA lands situated at Venkatala village was Rs.1,500/- per Square feet and added 50% on the guidance value by holding that the subject lands are abutting National Highway.

The respondent No. 2 again added 25% on the guidance value and arrived at the rate of Rs.2,625/- per Sq. feet i.e., Rs. 1,500/- per Sq. feet + Rs. 750/- per Square feet (50% of Rs. 1500/-) +
Rs. 375/- (25% of Rs. 1,500/-) = Rs. 2,625/- per Square feet.
.10.
The said enhancement has been challenged by the petitioner in this petition.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent No. 2 without considering the relevant provisions A.P.
No.129/2021 of NHA Act and also without considering the guidance value or market value of the property as on the date of Preliminary Notification enhanced the compensation by relying on the guidance value of the year 2009 published vide notification bearing No. CVC/19/2010-11 dated 21.09.2011.
The petitioner also claimed that the Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009.

As such,
the respondent No. 2 ought to have considered the market value of the property of the year 2009 and not of the year 2011.
As the aforesaid notification relied by the Arbitrator came to effect from 2011 i.e., after lapse of more than a year from the date of publication of Preliminary Notification.
Accordingly claimed that the said enhancement cannot be accepted.

It is true that as per the NH Act,
the market value of the land as on the date of Preliminary Notification has to be considered.

sentences.text: The petitioner also claimed that whatever the document relied by the respondent No. 2 for enhancing the compensation is not brought to the notice of the petitioner before passing the award/judgment.
Accordingly, claimed that such award is liable to be set aside as per Section 24 of National Highways Authority Act.

In this context, the petitioner relied on the decision reported A.P.
No.129/2022 in (2019) 15 SCC 131 in a case of Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs. National Highways Authority of India.

entities.text: Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs. National Highways Authority of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is true that in the said decision, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that whatever the document relied by the Arbitrator shall be brought to the notice of the parties, so that the parties can make submission or give a rebuttal evidence about such documents.
However, in the case on hand, such notification is not found in the record received from the Arbitrator.

.12 . It is the claim of the petitioner in the petition that as per the Special Instructions to the notification dated 21.09.2011, it provides that the properties adjacent to National and State Highways for which rates have not been fixed in the rate list, additional rate of 50% and 25% of other properties shall be fixed respectively and claimed that if the rate is not fixed for the properties adjacent to the properties of National Highways, the Arbitrator can enhance the price at 50% and in case of State Highways, additional rate of 25% can be fixed, but 75% cannot be enhanced.

The claim of the petitioner is that the Arbitrator / respondent No. 2 enhanced 75% of the market value, which is permissible and accordingly claimed that the enhancement cannot A.P. No.129/2021 be accepted.
Admittedly, the SLAO fixed the market value to the acquired property is Rs.1,314/- and that has been enhanced to Rs.2,625/- per Sq. feet by adding Rs.1,311/- per Sq. feet.
If the said enhancement is accepted, certainly it is clear that the respondent No. 2 enhanced the market value to the tune of 75%.
Hence, it is for the Arbitrator to give reasons on what basis 75% of the market value has been enhanced.
.13. The only reason assigned by the respondent No. 2 for enhancement of 75% is the discretion.
Now it is well settled principle of law that discretion must be used in judicially and not arbitrarily.

Admittedly as observed by the respondent No. 2 in its order as well as claimed by the petitioner in the petition that the Arbitrator can enhance 50% of the market value, if the market value of the acquired property besides National Highways is not found in or fixed in the rate list.
As such, only 50% of the market value can be enhanced by the SLAO and not more than that.
If at all the Arbitrator is enhancing another 25%, that is totally 75%, then there must be special reasons why the Arbitrator is enhancing 25% of the market value.
Such reasons are not found in the order of the Arbitrator / respondent No. 2.
When such a A.P. No.129/2022 case, certainly said enhancement cannot be accepted.

It is also not made out by the respondent No. 2 in its order that the property of respondent No. 1 has been acquired, has not found in the rate list, as such, the Arbitrator has added additional rate of 50% along with 25%.
Further the value of the property has been enhanced as per the notification of the year 2011, which is also not the part of records received from the Arbitrator.
Further, no such case is made out by the respondent No. 1 before the respondent No. 2 in the Arbitration proceedings.

Therefore, it is clear that the award passed by the Arbitrator is patently illegal and against the statutory provisions of Substantive Law that is in force and the award passed by the Arbitrator also leads to draw adverse inference under Section 24 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act as the documents relied by the Arbitrator not found in the records received from the Arbitrator.

The Arbitrator relied on the guidance value of the year 2011 that came to effect from National Highways Authority Of India vs Thirunagendra N on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79249631/
5 01.04.2011 and the land involved in this case acquired one year prior to the said date and also the Arbitrator has not given any specific reason for enhancement of 25% as claimed in the year.

sentences.text:
As such,
certainly the award passed by the Arbitrator is A.P. No.129/2021 patently illegal.
It is well settled principle of law that if the award passed by the Arbitrator is patently illegal, then such award should be set aside.

.14. In the case on hand, though the respondents 1 to 3 served with the notice not chosen to appear before the court to resist the case of the petition or to support the award passed by the respondent No. 2.
Absolutely no material placed before the court to disbelieve the petition case or to substantiate the award passed by the respondent No. 2.
Hence, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to intervene with the award passed by the Arbitrator and the award is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, the point No. 1 is held in the affirmative.
.15. Point No.2:
In view of my above finding, I proceed to pass the following.
ORDER  Petition filed under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act is hereby allowed.

A.P. No.129/2022  Consequently, the award passed by the  Arbitrator / respondent No. 2 in case No.
LAQ/ARB/NH-07/CR/33/2012-13 dated 22.01.2021 pertaining to Sy. No.25/4A measuring 606.80 Sq. feet of Venkatala village is set aside with a liberty to the parties to pursue their remedy in accordance with law.
Office is directed to send back the Lower Court Records.
